implementations.title: Agent sessions — who is running right now
implementations.summary: Lists the agent sessions running right now across every provider, behind an adapter seam so a new provider is a new file rather than a new branch.

implementations.title: The canvas — a command palette over a window canvas
implementations.summary: Replaces the removed terminal surface with a browser one — a command palette over draggable windows, where a pinned window re-runs itself on a Python-side cadence.

implementations.title: Capture — named formats: parse, transform, present
implementations.summary: Lets the operator declare a foreign tool's output structure by name in formats.toml, so `sb data --from` can table it without sky.boss ever inferring columns.

implementations.title: Chrome — what a window knows about its output
implementations.summary: Gives a window a band stating what it knows about its own output — quiet, late, dead — so silence and death stop looking alike.

implementations.title: Once, later — a delayed run you can watch
implementations.summary: Adds `sb run --delay 5m`: one run, later, behind a countdown you can cancel.

implementations.title: Following a file — the native cursor
implementations.summary: Follows a file with a native stat cursor so quiet and dead are different words, and `--due` makes late a word too.

implementations.title: Following a command, and live output for everything
implementations.summary: The streaming substrate: holds a command's stream open, treats any exit as a visible death, and gives every surface live output.

implementations.title: The mark — a header for `sb`
implementations.summary: Draws the sky.boss mark from one source so the CLI header, the README banner and the app icon cannot drift apart.

implementations.title: Highlight — lexical tint for followed lines
implementations.summary: Tints a followed line by shape rather than by severity, and lets the operator declare their own vocabulary without repainting sky.boss's.

implementations.title: History — how did this go the last seven nights
implementations.summary: Reads a declared project's own run ledger newest-first — the only observe that looks backwards.

implementations.title: Jobs — sky.boss issues a schedule of its own
implementations.summary: Gives sky.boss a schedule of its own with systemd as the daemon, and enforces the act/observe split per subcommand rather than per group.

implementations.title: Reading a file of records as data
implementations.summary: Reads a file of records as data, dispatching on argument shape, and reports record variance instead of acting on it.

implementations.title: The MCP surface — the tools, offered to an agent
implementations.summary: Speaks MCP on stdio so an agent gets the same observes the operator does, and nothing that acts.

implementations.title: Refresh, spelled the same everywhere
implementations.summary: Settles what a cadence means on every path, including a stream of NDJSON envelopes when there is no terminal to draw in.

implementations.title: Roll-call — many projects, one answer
implementations.summary: Asks every declared project how it is and folds the answers without inventing a status vocabulary of its own.

implementations.title: The schedule view
implementations.summary: Draws what fires next across projects and sky.boss's own jobs, ordered by an instant Python parsed and the page never re-reads.

implementations.title: Adopting skeletor as a scaffold
implementations.summary: Converts sky.boss from a skeletor component consumer into a scaffolded tree, and records what a fork can and cannot learn about itself.

implementations.title: The agent-state root
implementations.summary: Teaches sky.boss where agent state lives and adds `<project>:<path>` as an address rather than a command.

implementations.title: The subprocess boundary — what a command sky.boss runs inherits
implementations.summary: Defines what a command sky.boss spawns inherits: the operator's environment minus the two variables the wrapper added.

implementations.title: Table views — shaping a foreign CLI's JSON into a table worth reading
implementations.summary: The shaping contract — a view describes data and never filters it, decided in Python so both renderers draw what they are told.

implementations.title: Reading a tool that has no `--json`
implementations.summary: Shows what a command printed, verbatim, for tools with no `--json`, and refuses to infer columns from whitespace.

implementations.title: The tools — commands the operator saves
implementations.summary: The operator's saved commands: one block per tool, spliced rather than rewritten, with the surface allowed to write.

implementations.title: Unwatched — what a resident command can say with no band to say it in
implementations.summary: What a resident command may say with no band to say it in — bounded ticks, one line per lapse, and a refusal where there is nothing to count.

implementations.title: Workbench — where a command gets made
implementations.summary: A second screen where a command is authored rather than invoked: the contract is asserted, the argv drafted, and a trial run draws the real envelope.

implementations.title: Wrap — a followed line that fits the window
implementations.summary: Wraps a followed line to the window with a hanging indent, which is why a rendered line is a block rather than a span plus a newline.
